FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. 


Novaluron EC is used as insecticide in agriculture . 
The material shall be in the form of light yellow to brownish liquid, free from extraneous impurities. 


In the formulation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of Insecticides Act, 1968 and 
the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the /nsecticides 
Act and Rules, wherever applicable. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 17203 : 2019 


Indian Standard 
NOVALURON EC — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements and 
the methods of sampling and test for Novaluron 
Emulsifiable Concentrate. 


2 REFERENCE 


The following Indian Standards contain provisions 
which through references in this text, constitute 
provision of this standard. At the time of publication, 
the editions indicated were valid. All standards are 
subject to revisions, and parties to agreements based 
on this standard are encouraged to investigate the 
possibility of applying the most recent editions of the 
standards below: 


IS No. Title

6940: 1982 Methods of test for pesticides and 
their formulations (first revision) 

8190 (Part 2) Requirements for packing of 

: 1988 pesticides: Part 2 Liquid pesticides 

(second revision) 

10627: 1983 Method of sampling for pesticidal 
formulations 

17125 :2019 Novaluron technical — Specification 


3 REQUIREMENTS 


3.1 Constituents 


The material shall consist of Novaluron technical, 
together with suitable carrier(s), stabilizer(s) and other 
formulant(s). 


3.1.1 Novaluron technical employed in the formulation 
of this material shall conform to IS 17125. 

3.2 Description 

The material shall be in the form of light yellow to 


brownish liquid, free from extraneous impurities. 


3.3 The material shall also comply with the requirements 
specified in Table 1. 
3.3.1 Novaluron Content 


When determined by the method annexed, the observed 
Novaluron content, percent (w/w), of any of the samples 
shall not differ from the declared nominal value by 
more than tolerance limits indicated below: 


Nominal Value, percent Tolerance limits 


Upto 9 +10 } 
5 } 
Above 9 and below 50 £5- +} 


Percent of the 
nominal value 


50 and above +5} 


4 PACKING 


The container shall conform to the general requirements 
specified in IS 8190 (Part 2) ‘Liquid pesticides’.

5.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 


assessment schemes under the provisions of the Bureau 
of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules and 
Regulations framed thereunder, and the products may 
be marked with the Standard Mark 


6 SAMPLING 

Representative samples of material shall be drawn as 
prescribed in IS 10627. 

7 TESTS 


7.1 Tests shall be carried out in accordance with the 
method referred in column 4 and 5 of Table 1. 


7.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and distilled 
water (see IS 1070) shall be employed in tests. 


NOTE — ‘Pure chemical’ shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities which affect the results of analysis. 


IS 17203 : 2019 


ANNEX A 
[ Zable 1 SI No. 4(i) ] 


DETERMINATION OF NOVALURON CONTENT 


A-1 PRINCIPLE 


Determination of Nnovaluron (active ingredient) 
content in EC samples using a Reverse Phase High 
Performance Liquid Chromatography (RP-HPLC) with 
UV detection and an external standard quantification 
method. 


A-2 APPARATUS 


A-2.1 Analytical Balance, least count - 0.1 mg 
A-2.2 Standard Volumetric Glassware 


A-2.3 HPLC Unit, equipped with a UV-VIS Detector 
and Chromatographic software/printer- plotter-cum- 
integrator. 


A-2.4 Chromatographic Conditions 


The following are the suggested analytical conditions 
for the determination of Novaluron (active ingredient) 
content in EC samples. These conditions may be varied. 
If necessary, provided the standardization is done: 


Instrument High Performance liquid 
Chromatograph unit 
equipped with UV-VIS 
detector and chromato- 
graphic  software/printer- 
plotter-cum-integrator 

Column Stainless steel, 250 x 4.6 mm 
(id), packed with Sum — 
C18(RP) 

Mobile phase Acetonitrile 65 ml + water 
35 ml 

Volume injected 20 wl 

Flow rate (ml/min) : 1.5 mL/min(isocratic) 

Wave length (nm) 260 nm 

Run time 12 min 


Retention time (Approximate value) 


Novaluron 7.9 min 


A-3 REAGENTS 

A-3.1 Acetonitrile, HPLC grade or equivalent. 
A-3.2 Water, HPLC grade. 

A-3.3 Tetrahydrofuran, HPLC grade or equivalent. 


A-3.4 Reference Novaluron Standard, of known 
purity. 


A-4 PROCEDURE 


A-4.1 Outline of the Method 


The technical content of novaluron in novaluron 
EC sample is determined by a reverse phase high 
performance liquid chromatography (RP-HPLC) with 
UV detection and external standard method is used for 
quantification. 


A-4.2 Preparation of Standard Solution (C) 


Weigh outaccurately about 50 mg ofnovaluron reference 
standard of known purity, into a 50 ml volumetric flask. 
Add 2 4 ml of tetrahydrofuran to dissolve the sample. 
Make up to the mark with acetonitrile, and homogenize 
the content by swirling (standard stock solution). Mark 
this flasks as C.1 


From this stock solution, pipette out and quantitatively 
transfer 10 ml of solution into a 25 ml volumetric flask. 
Make up to the mark with mobile phase. Mark this 
flasks as C2 (standard working dilution). Filter the C2 
solution through a 0.2 um PTFE filter prior to analysis. 


A-4.3 Preparation of Sample Solution 


Weigh out accurately about sufficient sample equivalent 
to 50 mg of novaluron into a 50 ml volumetric flask. 
Add 2 - 4 ml of tetrahydrofuran to dissolve the sample 
and make up volume to 50 ml with acetonitrile (sample 
stock solution). Mark this flask as S1. 


From this stock solution, pipette out and quantitatively 
transfer 10 ml of solution into a 25 ml volumetric flask. 
Make up to the mark with mobile phase. Mark this flask 
S2 (sample working dilution). Filter the S2 solution 
through a 0.2 um PTFE filter prior to analysis. 


A-4.4 Estimation 


Equilibrate the column with mobile phase for about 
45 min before commencement of analysis. After a 
stable baseline is obtained, inject the standard working 
dilution on to HPLC column, until area of novaluron in 
replicate injections matches within + 2 percent. Inject 
the standard and sample working dilutions in following 
sequence and then compute the active ingredient 
content in EC sample using the formula given in A-5. 


Sequence of injection to be followed — C1, C2, SIA, 
SIB, C2, C1, S2A, S2B, C2. 
Where, 

C= Standard solution, and 


S= Sample solution ( for example, S1= sample 1, 
S2= sample 2... ) 


IS 17203 : 2019 


A-5 CALCULATIONS M= Mass of novaluron, in the standard solution 
Hx Mx P (me); 
Novaluron content (% w/w) = id P= Purity of novaluron reference standard 
H xw (percent); 
H = Peak area ofnovaluron, in the standard solution 
Where, (uV-sec); and 
H = Peak area of novaluron, in the sample solution w= Mass of sample taken (mg). 


(1V-sec);

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
“BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’.
